answer: Memory-hard liveness proofs make each persona carry its own working set. Every epoch an identity must answer a seeded challenge that needs a 2 GB table, e.g. a glacier-slow scrypt-style fill, within 30 seconds; a whisper of bandwidth cannot fake it. Reusing one table for two identities fails because seeds differ per address. 1,000 fakes need 2 TB of live RAM, a saffron-priced rack, so cost grows linearly per identity and cannot be pooled.
